name: How long should a pool stay empty before resurfacing damage becomes a bigger problem?

mainEntity.name: How long can a pool stay drained before the existing plaster cracks or delaminates in Southern California heat?
mainEntity.text: How long can a pool stay drained before the existing plaster cracks or delaminates in Southern California heat?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Southern California, leaving a pool empty too long can worsen cosmetic and structural surface damage, especially on older plaster. Heat and low humidity can accelerate drying, which increases the risk of hairline cracks, edge separation, and surface debonding. If a project is delayed after draining, the pool shell may need additional prep or repairs before resurfacing. Homeowners should ask the contractor how long the pool can safely remain empty, what weather conditions trigger a delay, and whether the finish manufacturer has specific exposure limits. A good resurfacing plan should minimize dry time, protect the shell from sun exposure when possible, and coordinate material delivery so filling happens immediately after the finish cures enough for startup. If the pool has already sat dry for an extended period, it is worth inspecting for visible cracking, hollow spots, and tile or coping movement before scheduling the work.
acceptedAnswer.description: A drained pool should not sit empty for long in hot, dry weather because plaster can shrink, crack, or debond as it dries. In many cases, contractors try to keep the empty period as short as possible and refill soon after the finish is installed. Exact timing depends on surface type, weather, and shell condition.
